source.units: inch (OCCT converts to mm on import)

rotation_convention: build123d Location.orientation: intrinsic XYZ Euler angles, degrees; rebuild with Location(position, rotation_xyz_deg). matrix_3x4 = rows of the gp_Trsf (rotation | translation) for other consumers.
frames: rel = relative to the parent node (what assemblies/*.py compose); world = arm frame. A record with a `mount` block (keys under `mounted`) is a motor mount declared in lib/mounts.py, not a SolidWorks node: parent None, rel == world = host world * mount frame.

solidworks.note: the SolidWorks node (imported from the drive repo's export.py assembly: ring pins z 4.5 / output pins z 13, no fasteners) - cross-check only; the module's contents come from assemblies/cycloidal_drive.py

mount.note: the base's other half (its plate the motor's seat), bolted to the base's posts at the joint face; built in the base's part frame
the mount's 4x M4 x screw_len: heads on its posts' inner faces, along -X through its posts and the base's
the screws' nuts in the base posts' hex pockets, their outer faces flush with the posts' back faces, a corner up
the motor-side leg on j1_coupler's disc, round the drive's motor sleeve; built in the coupler's part frame
the drive's output hub to j1_coupler's hub-side leg: 4x M4 x hub_screw_len, the heads in the leg's counterbores, along the drive's axis through the leg and the hub's arm-mount holes
the hub screws' nuts captive in the hub's flange, on their pockets' floors (hub_nut_depth), a corner toward its axis
j1_motor_leg's foot to j1_coupler's disc: 2x M4 x motor_screw_len, the heads in the foot's counterbores, along the drive's axis through the foot and the disc's wall
the foot screws' nuts in the disc's slots, against their outer walls (motor_nut_wall), a corner up the slot
j1_motor_leg's ring to the drive's motor plate's sleeve: 3x M4 x sleeve_screw_len radially at sleeve_bolt_deg, the heads on the ring's od
the sleeve screws' nuts pressed into the sleeve's lugs, on their pockets' floors, a corner along the tangent

the 48 mm motor under the motor mount's plate (in the base's part frame), shaft up through it, on its round holes; motor + board end BASE_MOTOR_TABLE_CLEAR above the base's bottom face; connector toward +X [ESTIMATE]

on the web across j1_link's motor hole (on its 4 holes), ELBOW_MOTOR_CENTRES short of the elbow axis, the body +N down the hole through the slab, shaft -N through the web; connector toward -Z [ESTIMATE] (toward the elbow the roll block would pass it 0.2 mm off)

on j2_link's web (+Z face), shaft -N, on round holes at J2_MOTOR_X (WRIST_MOTOR_CENTRES from the wrist); connector sideways toward j2_link's -Y - away from the elbow axis once the forearm is turned -, its plug's room beside the motor (toward the wall it would come within the plug's room of the wall)
the elbow motor's 20T on its shaft, hub toward the motor, J1_MOTOR_20T_HUB_Z out from its face (under the web): its tooth band level with the elbow 90T's
the base_yaw motor's 20T on its shaft, its hub in the motor plate's window: its tooth band level with the 120T's
the wrist motor's 20T on its shaft, its hub up in the web's pilot slot: its tooth band level with the wrist 90T's
the elbow motor's 4x M3 x J1_MOTOR_SCREW_LEN SHCS (the drive motor's): heads flush in the pockets in the underside of the web across j1_link's motor hole, up through it into the motor's tapped holes
the wrist motor's 4x M3 x J2_MOTOR_SCREW_LEN SHCS (the elbow motor's): heads flush in the counterbores in the underside of j2_link's web, up through it into the motor's tapped holes

the base_yaw motor's 4x M3 x YAW_MOTOR_SCREW_LEN SHCS (the roll motor's): heads flush in the counterbores in the top of the motor mount's plate, down through it and its pad into the motor's tapped holes
the base's bore (axis +Y): the upper (coupler-side) 6806, on the lip
the base's bore (axis +Y): the lower (pulley-side) 6806, under the lip
j1_link's elbow bore (axis +Y; slid with the elbow end): the upper (coupler-side) 6806, on the lip
j1_link's elbow bore (axis +Y; slid with the elbow end): the lower (pulley-side) 6806, under the lip
j2_link's wrist boss (axis +Z): the upper (coupler-side) 6806, on the lip
j2_link's wrist boss (axis +Z): the lower (pulley-side) 6806, under the lip
the thrust bearing's lower washer, on the floor of the base's groove
the needle cage on the lower washer, round the base's seat ring
the upper washer, under j1_coupler's seat (its recess's ceiling) - it turns with the coupler

the elbow 90T, PULLEY_SEAT_SHIFT out from its SolidWorks pose (retired): its hub in the lower elbow bearing; turned pulley_bolt_deg about its axis with the block's bolt pattern (the nut channels clear of the ring cavity)

the wrist 90T, PULLEY_SEAT_SHIFT out from its SolidWorks pose (retired): its hub in the lower wrist bearing; turned pulley_bolt_deg about its axis with wrist_link's bolt pattern (the front nut clear of the post's flat)

the base_yaw 120T under j1_coupler, hub up: its hub end on the stub's end, its journal in the lower base bearing, its ring under that bearing's inner ring (it holds the coupler down on the thrust bearing); turned hole_deg about its axis onto the stub's diagonal holes
the elbow 90T's 4x M4 x pulley_screw_len: heads in its counterbores, down through its hub and the block's stub
the elbow screws' nuts on the block's channel seats (nut_seat_x), a flat toward the axis
the wrist 90T's 4x M4 x pulley_screw_len: heads in its counterbores, down through its hub and wrist_link's stub
the wrist screws' nuts on wrist_link's channel seats (nut_seat_z, level with the upper wrist bearing's top, as the elbow's), turned with the 90T
the base_yaw 120T's 4x M4 x pulley_screw_len: heads in its counterbores (under it), up through its hub and j1_coupler's stub
the base_yaw screws' nuts in j1_coupler's hex pockets, flush with the floor of the pocket over its hub (nut_depth under pocket_y0), a corner along the coupler's Z
the base_yaw belt inside the base: the motor's 20T to the 120T under j1_coupler, round its idler
the elbow belt under j1_link's web: the elbow motor's 20T to the elbow 90T
the wrist belt under j2_link's web: the wrist motor's 20T to the wrist 90T
the elbow belt's tensioner under j1_link's slab, level with the belt, on its back on the 90T -> 20T run
its printed spacer: the land on the idler's inner ring, the riser on the slab's underside
its M5 axle: the head under the idler, up through the idler, the spacer and the floor's slot into the nut
its nut on the floor of its slot down from the slab's top face, its flats across the link's X
the base_yaw belt's tensioner on the motor mount's plate, level with the belt, on its back on the 120T -> 20T run
its printed spacer: the land under the idler's inner ring, the riser on the mount's plate
its M5 axle: the head on the idler, down through the idler, the spacer and the plate's slot into the nut
its nut on the plate's underside between the rails, its flats across the slot
the wrist belt's tensioner under j2_link's web, level with the belt, on its back on the run leaving the motor's 20T
its M5 axle: the head under the idler, up through the idler, the rib and the web's slot into the nut
its nut on the floor of its channel down from the web's top face, its flats across j2_link's x

the roll drive on j2_link's roll axis (y 0, z FOREARM_ROLL_AXIS_Z), in its frame before the forearm's turn: module +Z = host -X toward the wrist, module +X = host +Z (N), +Y = up in the swing plane (the motor side); the block IS the elbow coupler: its stub turns in j1_link's bore and the elbow 90T bolts into it (j3_coupler#1 retired, lib/placements.py RETIRED)

the wrist roll drive on wrist_link's roll axis R' (WRIST_ROLL_OFFSET along -Y from the pitch axis - WristRollParams.side -, WRIST_ROLL_AXIS_H over the plate's coupler face): module +Z = host +X toward the gripper, module +X = host -Z (away from the plate), +Y = host +Y (from R' toward the pancake); wrist_link IS its frame (the stator), the pancake and its 20T replace nema17_pancake#1 / gt2_pulley_20t#1 (lib/placements.py RETIRED); beyond the forearm's turn, it turns with wrist_link

the rack & pinion gripper on the wrist roll's axis R' at gripper_j3_connector's plate (the connector bolted to the roll pulley's face): module +Z along R' toward the fingertips, +Y the jaws' travel - the connector's plate's long axis, connector_turn_deg - 180 about R' from the drive's +Y; it replaces the SolidWorks gripper (lib/reference.py SKIPPED_PRODUCTS); beyond the forearm's turn, it turns with wrist_link
